name: Magnesium glycinate

lead: Magnesium glycinate is magnesium bound to glycine, about 14 percent elemental magnesium, sold to correct deficiency and popular for sleep, relaxation and recovery. Looksmaxxing users take it for deeper sleep, which they link to fresher skin, less puffiness and better training.

It supplies magnesium, a mineral involved in many enzyme and nerve functions, with glycine, which proponents say adds a calming effect. Marketing describes it as gentler and better absorbed than oxide forms; trials on glycinate specifically for sleep are few, and many sleep claims rest on magnesium in general or on stacks with theanine and GABA.

paras: People take it as capsules or powder in the evening, usually as part of a wind-down routine and often combined with other sleep supplements. Users report changes in sleep and relaxation within days to a few weeks.
Diarrhoea is the main reported effect and is described as milder than with other forms. Severe renal impairment is listed as a contraindication in reference text.

angle.text: Magnesium glycinate is popular for calmer sleep, relaxation and recovery, which users tie to a more rested face and better training. Sleep claims often rest on magnesium in general or on stacks with theanine and GABA, with few glycinate-specific trials.

lead: Magnesium glycinate, also called magnesium bisglycinate or diglycinate, is the magnesium salt of glycine, containing about 14.1 percent elemental magnesium by mass [1]. It is sold as a supplement to relieve magnesium deficiency and also appears in cosmetics [1]. Marketing often presents it as better tolerated and more absorbable than magnesium oxide, and it is popular for sleep, relaxation and recovery [2].

Wikipedia does not address absorption, evidence or adverse effects [1]. Human studies comparing magnesium compounds exist, but trials specifically on glycinate for sleep or appearance are limited in the sources reviewed here.

paras: The main stated use is addressing or preventing magnesium deficiency [1]. Reference text also lists proposed uses for sleep quality, anxiety, muscle soreness and migraines, which is a description of claims rather than established findings [2].
A 2019 study investigated dose-dependent absorption of different magnesium compounds [3]. The article is a comparison of compounds; specific glycinate results are not summarised here.

Randomised trials of combined magnesium and vitamin D supplementation have examined vitamin D status, inflammation and blood pressure, and separately bone turnover and glycaemic control (the latter reporting no influence) [4][5]. Newer reports include a randomised study of glycinate as add-on therapy in hypomagnesaemic asthma and COPD, and a case report of high-dose glycinate in severe hypomagnesaemia [6]. A rat study examined chronic glycinate effects on intestinal motility [7]. Registered trials examine magnesium for insomnia [8] and in athletes for sleep and recovery [9], with no published outcomes in these sources.
Reference text states diarrhoea is the main reported effect, described as less frequent than with other magnesium forms, and severe renal impairment is listed as a contraindication [2].
